A01.truthBoundary: Validates exact input structure, digests and provenance fields. It does not independently verify the explorer/provider or customer rights.

A02.truthBoundary: Compares supplied runtime bytecodes exactly or after strict Solidity CBOR metadata stripping. It does not execute the compiler or resolve immutables/libraries automatically.

A03.truthBoundary: Produces a deterministic preliminary threat model; qualified human architecture review remains mandatory.

A04.truthBoundary: Maps source/ABI privilege surfaces but cannot prove current on-chain role holders, multisig, timelock or hidden implementation behavior.

A05.truthBoundary: Two separate local code paths execute over source and ABI/bytecode lanes. They are not substitutes for two validated external analyzer families or independent assurance.

bytecodeComparison.truthBoundary: A match proves equality of supplied runtime bytecode under the stated normalization only; source compilation and chain retrieval remain separate evidence lanes.

findings.title: Privileged ABI surface: pause()
findings.description: The ABI exposes a pause control surface. ABI presence does not prove who can call it or whether delay/multisig controls exist.
findings.safeRemediation: Bind the function to source-level authorization, owner/role state, proxy administration and operational controls before rating it safe.
limitations: ABI-only observation; caller permissions and implementation behavior require source/state evidence.

findings.title: SELFDESTRUCT opcode present in deployed runtime
findings.description: SELFDESTRUCT was found by push-aware bytecode traversal at program counter 25. Presence alone does not prove exploitability.
findings.safeRemediation: Trace reachable callers and targets, verify authorization and state assumptions, then add path, invariant and fork tests.
limitations: Opcode presence only; no control-flow graph or path feasibility analysis.

findings.title: Delegatecall execution surface
findings.description: Delegatecall executes foreign code in the caller storage context and requires exact target, upgrade and storage-layout controls.
findings.safeRemediation: Bind allowed implementations, protect upgrades, document storage layout and test unauthorized target substitution.
limitations: Local lexical/structural heuristic; no path feasibility proof and no human adjudication.

findings.safeRemediation: Bound iteration, paginate work or enforce a maximum collection size and test worst-case gas.

findings.title: Authorization depends on tx.origin
findings.description: tx.origin can make authorization depend on the entire call chain rather than the immediate caller.
findings.safeRemediation: Use explicit role or msg.sender-based authorization and test calls through intermediary contracts.
limitations: Local lexical/structural heuristic; no path feasibility proof and no human adjudication.

findings.title: Destructive opcode source surface
findings.description: The source exposes a destructive lifecycle operation whose current chain semantics and authorization must be reviewed.
findings.safeRemediation: Remove the operation where possible or require explicit governance, delay, monitoring and chain-specific behavior tests.
limitations: Local lexical/structural heuristic; no path feasibility proof and no human adjudication.
